Cook to the cited temperature threshold rather than to the clock alone.
summary: Salmon fillets laid among sweet potato, peppers and onion for the last ten minutes of a vegetable roast. The fish goes in whole and untouched — no turning, no skinning, no pan work — which is what makes it a reasonable first fish dish.

ingredients.note: Fish allergen. The source leaves the skin on and sets it against the pan.

ingredients.item: Sweet potato, cut into 1 cm cubes
Bell peppers, cut into pieces about 2 cm by 2 cm
Small red onions, peeled and cut into wedges

ingredients.note: For the vegetables. The source drizzles a little extra over the salmon and marks that as optional.

ingredients.quantity: The source seasons to taste and gives no weight.

method.instruction: Heat the oven to 220°C conventional, or 200°C fan (gas mark 7). Both figures are stated by the source; neither is a conversion made here.
Spread the sweet potato, peppers and onion over a very large roasting pan in a single layer.
Drizzle over the 2 tablespoons of oil, scatter the thyme, season, and turn everything to coat before spreading it flat again.
Take the pan out, stir the vegetables and spread them flat, then settle the four fillets among them with the skin against the pan. Drizzle with a little oil if you are using it, and season.

Roast for a further 10 minutes. The source's endpoint is whatever doneness you prefer, which is not a usable test on its own; for a cooked-through fillet Health Canada gives 70°C internal, measured at the thickest part. The source states no fillet thickness, only the 130 g weight, so go by the thermometer rather than by the clock.

yield_note: Serves 4, as stated by the source. Source times: 5 minutes preparation and 25 minutes cooking. The source gives no resting time, and none is invented here.

provenance_note: Recipe facts paraphrased from Eb Gargano's page at Easy Peasy Foodie, accessed 2026-09-14; the safety threshold is Health Canada's. The source's only endpoint for the fish is cooking it to your liking, which is not a usable instruction for a beginner on its own, so Health Canada's 70°C is given beside it and attributed. No fillet thickness is stated by the source; only the 130 g weight is. The source writes tablespoons without stating a millilitre value, so no spoon size is asserted here.

caveats: Fish has its own threshold, separate from the meat records in this collection: Health Canada gives 70°C internal for fish. Salmon is often served less cooked than that by choice; this record states the safe figure rather than a preference.
Raw fish and its packaging contaminate surfaces. Wash hands, board and knife after handling, and do not rest cooked fillets where the raw ones sat.
Allergen: fish. The dish contains no gluten or dairy as written, but check any seasoning you add.
